title: fixedTimeLimit appends the caller's stack to the callable's exception on every attempt, so a reused exception grows without bound (heap, CPU, logs, OOM)
cause: AttemptTimeLimiters.FixedAttemptTimeLimit.call (AttemptTimeLimiters.java:107) calls Guava's deprecated four-argument SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout(..., true); its failure path throwCause(e, true) (SimpleTimeLimiter.java:162-163, 256-259) calls setStackTrace on the exception object the callable threw, concatenating the caller thread's stack, and Retryer.call stores and rethrows that same object.
trigger: A Retryer built with AttemptTimeLimiters.fixedTimeLimit(...) runs a callable that fails more than once with the same exception object (a preallocated sentinel, a cheap exception that only overrides fillInStackTrace, or a memoised failed CompletableFuture whose join() rethrows the same CompletionException).
consequence: The reused exception gains one caller stack (caller depth + ~5 frames) per failed attempt and is never reset: RetryListener log entries and printed RetryExceptions grow linearly (129 -> 445,629 chars after 900 attempts), per-call CPU grows, and retained heap grows until OutOfMemoryError (under -Xmx32m call #1604 ends with ExecutionException(OutOfMemoryError) instead of RetryException); noTimeLimit leaves the exception unchanged.
premises: The Guava on the classpath is one guava-retrying 2.0.0 links against (10.x-22.0); in each, the four-argument SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout unwraps failures with throwCause(e, true), which calls cause.setStackTrace(concat(cause, caller stack)) (javap-checked for 10.0.1, 14.0.1, 16.0.1, 19.0, 22.0).
The callable throws the same exception object on more than one failed attempt, and that object's stack trace is writable (not built with writableStackTrace=false).
Nothing in the application resets the reused exception's stack trace between attempts.
